request: Hi , Please remove the fillet at the front center and add a 1 millimeter chamfer instead

actions.target: the front-side annular fillet surrounding the central carrier socket, identified as the Central hub blend in feature F005
actions.relational_constraint: The fillet is concentric with the rotational center and lies at the front center of the carrier. The semantic orientation maps the +Z view to the front with confidence 0.82. In that view, the applicable rounded annular transition is the toroidal Central hub blend, FACE 580, rather than the insert's existing conical lead-in or the spoke and rim blends.
steps: Activate SOLID 1 and isolate section R02, Carrier hub and spoke network; leave the separate central insert SOLID 0 unchanged.
Orient the model to the semantically identified front side corresponding to the +Z labeled view and locate the concentric rounded transition at the center of the carrier.
Select feature F005, Central carrier socket and hub transition, and identify FACE 580, the toroidal Central hub blend with major radius 14.896681 mm and minor radius 5.080000 mm.

If editable feature history is available, suppress or delete only the fillet operation that generated FACE 580 while retaining the underlying central socket, hub, spoke network, and planar front web geometry.
If operating as a direct STEP edit, remove FACE 580 and heal the resulting annular gap by extending and intersecting its adjacent parent surfaces to recover the sharp pre-fillet circular edge loop.
Confirm that the defeaturing operation affects only SOLID 1 and does not alter the separate central splined coupling insert R01, including its internal splines and external scalloped profile.
Recompute the body and verify that SOLID 1 remains a single valid solid and that a continuous sharp annular edge now exists at the former location of FACE 580.

actions.target: the restored annular edge loop at the front-center carrier socket where FACE 580 was removed
actions.relational_constraint: The new chamfer replaces the removed front-center fillet at the same concentric boundary in feature F005. It must be applied around the complete restored annular edge loop, not to the internal spline edges, the insert lead-in, the spoke openings, or the outer sprocket rim.
actions.unresolved_reference: The request supplies one chamfer size but no angle or second distance. Interpret it as a standard equal-distance 1 mm chamfer, nominally 1 mm by 1 mm at 45 degrees, unless the CAD system's project standard specifies a different one-distance convention.
steps: Use the healed sharp annular edge loop created by removal of FACE 580 as the chamfer edge selection; because model.json does not provide a B-rep EDGE index for this loop, identify it topologically as the complete boundary formerly occupied by FACE 580.
Create a chamfer feature on SOLID 1 after the fillet-removal or direct-healing operation.
Set the chamfer to 1.0 mm. Use an equal-distance 1.0 mm by 1.0 mm definition, producing a nominal 45-degree chamfer, because no second distance or angle was specified.
Propagate the selection around the full concentric edge loop so the chamfer is continuous around the front-center carrier socket.
Ensure the chamfer cuts back from the restored parent faces without extending onto the separate insert SOLID 0 or changing the socket's intended concentric relationship with R01.
Recompute the model and inspect the +Z front view and iso1 view to confirm that the former rounded annular center blend has been replaced by a straight-sided 1 mm chamfer.

Validate that both original solids remain valid and disconnected as intended, and confirm that the central socket, spoke network, outer rim, sprocket teeth, and internal spline interface retain their original dimensions and topology except at the specified transition.

intention: Replace the rounded front-center carrier hub transition with a small straight bevel while preserving the central coupling fit and all other sprocket geometry.
